verdict.rationale: Conductor's own docs show it runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode in parallel, each in an isolated worktree. Cloud agents run builds without step-by-step confirmation and keep working after you close your laptop, so the parallel, autonomous fleet core is directly supported. The 'for hours or days' part is only implied by cloud persistence and is never documented, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documented support for multi-hour or multi-day agent runs (session duration and limits), evidence of fleet-scale concurrency limits, independent or hands-on corroboration of long-running autonomous cloud agents.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can launch fleets of autonomous agents that work in parallel on different tasks for hours or days

citations.quote: Conductor lets you run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode in parallel.
That lets agents work in parallel without editing the same files on disk.
Sandboxes spin up in seconds, and agents keep working after you close your laptop.
The agent can test your repositories, update install and setup scripts, and run builds — without asking you to confirm each step.
Each task gets its own workspace, branch, files, terminal, diff, and review path.
